Rishi / Laura —  confirmed details below (keeping it high level for the customer, can share this wording):

1) Unit accounting (hosted API): all text generation endpoints are billed by tokens consumed unless specifically noted (e.g., embeddings or fine-tuning units). Tokens = encoded input tokens + generated output tokens.

2) Responses vs Chat Completions vs legacy completions: these are primarily API surface distinctions.
   - Responses: new ergonomic endpoint. Bills per-token (input + output). If you use tool-calls / function-calling there is currently no separate large per-call surcharge — only the token consumption and (rare) small platform request fee we apply to high-frequency tiny requests (shows as a separate line in invoices with SKU "platform-request-small").
   - Chat Completions (old): same token accounting; invoiced under a different SKU for historical/compatibility reasons.
   - Legacy completions: effectively same token model; the invoice UI may group it under a "legacy" SKU.

3) Streaming: tokens are counted as produced. If you stream partial tokens and cancel, only the tokens emitted up to cancelation are billed.

4) Examples for clarity:
   - Example A: single request with 150 input tokens and 850 generated tokens -> billed for 1000 tokens.
   - Example B (streaming): same as above if full stream emitted; if client cancels after 400 generated tokens, billed for 550 tokens.

5) Platform/request fees: small and rare; apply to high-frequency <200-token requests. Typical customers (conversational workloads) don't see this on every call.

6) Invoice presentation: because of historical SKU names we sometimes see both "responses" and "chat-completions" lines even when usage is interchangeable. We can provide a mapping table for accounting.

If helpful, I can export a per-call breakdown for Acme's account for the month so they can reconcile line-by-line.
